question: Can fixed low-order moments of the degree-r Frobenius fiber be reproduced by a short base-field Laurent calculation, and does one fixed frozen radix-six predicate return the scalar digit on every public toy target?

claims.text: Candidate and direct enumeration return identical 16-moment vectors on every in-domain target and coordinate isomorphism.
claims.if_supported: Exact finite identity support for the frozen cohort; generic theorem remains separate.
claims.if_not_supported: Retain the first mismatch and refute the frozen implementation claim.

claims.text: One predeclared predicate ID is exact across every frozen row and target.
claims.if_supported: Requires independent replay and a new held-out protocol before decoder use.
claims.if_not_supported: Record the complete score distribution; select no fallback family.

hypotheses.statement: The denominator-cancelled trace and residue formulas require only the first fixed Laurent coefficients of R.
hypotheses.mechanism: logarithmic-derivative denominator cancellation and partial-fraction residue extraction

hypotheses.statement: For fixed J=8, candidate online field-operation growth is polylogarithmic in p while direct enumeration grows with r.
hypotheses.mechanism: fixed-length Laurent recurrence versus explicit r-term extension-field sum

predictions.minimum_effect: candidate base-field operation total is below direct total on every selected curve

provenance.decisive_scope: finite component counts only; asymptotic statement needs proof

hypotheses.statement: At least one of 648 frozen public predicate IDs is exact on every row.
hypotheses.mechanism: one fixed cross-curve radix-six channel applied to scalar-blind moment vectors

predictions.minimum_effect: one ID is exact on every row and target

provenance.decisive_scope: discovery cohort only; held-out confirmation separately required

arms.description: Base-field normalized-isogeny Laurent recurrence plus relative trace and residue extraction, J=8.
Explicit extension-field construction of H=ker(V-1), all r fiber points and direct sums.

measurement.timed_primary_justification: Timing is secondary; exact identity and score counts are primary. L2 and A/A still gate any timing comparison.

stopping_rules.rule: Stop after the five deterministic curves, all rows/targets, one warmup and five measured rounds; retain every failure and missing row.
Stop affected scoring at the first candidate/direct mismatch, label implementation invalid, and retain the complete packet generated to that point.
Stop new launches when the 2 USD cumulative ceiling, 1800-second job deadline or two infrastructure attempts is exhausted.

invalidation_rules: Any scalar-label read before moment serialization invalidates the candidate packet.
Any selector deviation, H115 fixture collision, wrong group order, nonprime r, violated p>19 or extension bound invalidates the cohort.
Any moment mismatch, coordinate-isomorphism mismatch, missing operation count, binary/source/protocol hash mismatch or failed tamper test blocks scoring or timing admission.
A/A outside [0.90,1.10], failed L2, automatic scientific retry or heterogeneous host blocks timing claims but preserves exact counts.
No discovered predicate may be used on a held-out cohort without a new committed protocol.

decision_rule.text: Identity is supported within the finite scope only if mismatches=0 and all controls pass. A digit candidate exists only if one fixed ID is exact on every row and target; ties retain all IDs and require the same held-out rule. Otherwise report the full score distribution and no selected ID.
decision_rule.threshold: zero mismatches; exact predicate on every row and target
decision_rule.statistic: exact counts, plus median/range for admitted timing
decision_rule.interval: none for exact census; measured range for timing
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: absolute operation/time difference and ratio by phase; exact-row deficit from total

graphs: cold and online timing by r

inadmissible: hidden scalar use in candidate moment construction
unpriced kernel, extension, table, verification or recovery work
reporting an admitted component ratio as an end-to-end ECDLP ratio
claiming subexponential ECDLP from finite data without the named proof obligations
